answer: In an agent marketplace, each identity must lock a refundable stake before bidding for work, with each stake backing only one active account. An attacker trying to flood an orchard of service listings with fake agents must lock more capital for every account. Even if the stakes are returned, that capital cannot fund an oasis of legitimate activity or a glacier monitoring project in the meantime. The resulting opportunity cost makes a large sybil swarm expensive, though not impossible.
